related_questions.question: Why was the US inflation rate so high in 2022?
related_questions.snippet: As the labor market tightened during 2021 and 2022, core inflation rose as the ratio of job vacancies to unemployment increased. This ratio is used to measure wage pressures that then pass through to the prices for goods and services. As workers bargain for better pay, firms begin to increase prices.

related_questions.question: What is the highest inflation rate in US history?

text_blocks.snippet: The highest recorded annual inflation rate in US history, based on the Consumer Price Index (CPI), was 23.7% in June 1920. This period of high inflation followed World War I.

While the highest rate occurred in 1920, the US has experienced other periods of significant inflation, particularly during and after World War I and in the late 1970s. In 1917, the inflation rate was 20.49%. The 1970s also saw high inflation, with the decade averaging 6.8%, more than double the long-run historical average. In 1980, the inflation rate was 13.55%.

text_blocks.snippet: In 2022, the US experienced a significant surge in inflation, with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rising 6.5% from December 2021 to December 2022. This increase was largely driven by rising food and energy prices, as well as durable goods. The 12-month increase in the CPI reached 9.1% in June 2022, marking the largest increase in 40 years, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
